questions.q: What is the key difference between NTFS permissions and share permissions?
options: NTFS permissions apply whether access is local or over the network; share permissions only apply when accessing a resource through its network share
Share permissions apply everywhere, while NTFS permissions only apply over the network
They are two names for the exact same thing
NTFS permissions only apply to printers, not folders
questions.explain: NTFS permissions live on the file system itself and apply regardless of access method. Share permissions are a separate layer that only matters when connecting through the network share.

questions.q: Which NTFS permission level allows viewing file contents and running executables, but not making changes?
options: Read & Execute
Full Control
Modify
Write
questions.explain: Read & Execute allows viewing contents and running executables without allowing changes. Modify adds write/delete, and Full Control adds permission changes and ownership.

questions.q: How many standard levels does share permission have, compared to NTFS?
options: Share permissions have three levels (Full Control, Change, Read); NTFS has five
Both have exactly five levels
Share permissions have five levels; NTFS has three
Neither has a fixed number of levels
questions.explain: Share permissions are a simpler layer with only three levels: Full Control, Change, and Read. NTFS has five: Full Control, Modify, Read & Execute, Read, and Write.

questions.q: When a user accesses a folder over the network, and NTFS and share permissions disagree, what determines the user's actual access?
options: The more restrictive of the two effective permissions wins
The share permission always wins
The NTFS permission always wins
Whichever permission was set most recently wins
questions.explain: Windows combines each layer's Allow permissions into an effective permission, then applies whichever of the two layers is more restrictive.

questions.q: In the worked example, Finance-Employees has Change on the share and Read & Execute on NTFS. What can Jordan Lee actually do when connecting over the network?
options: Open and run files, but not save changes or delete anything, because NTFS's Read & Execute is more restrictive than the share's Change
Freely edit and delete files, because Change allows it
Nothing at all, because the two permissions conflict and block access entirely
Only view a list of filenames, with no ability to open any file
questions.explain: Since the more restrictive permission wins, Jordan's effective access is Read & Execute — he can open and run files but cannot write or delete, despite the share allowing Change.
